author: /root/recovery
tracking: Root owns Beads; this private design receipt is not a parallel issue tracker.
recommendation: Dispatch a bounded internal staged-envelope activation coordinator under29.2.2 next; keep public app/provider/session routing and legacy v1 replacement migration separate. Do not expose activate(Prepared) or auto-resume based on files.
closed_work_preserved: 29.1 preparation remains stage-only and v1-source-only; the Prepared UUID is evidence, not a capability.
29.2.1 decodeActive supports v2 while legacy decode and original refusal regression remain unchanged.
Read-only proof, WAL handling, admission poison, retained evidence, immutable v2 reader and all existing test identities remain intact.

current_v1_risks.finding: Deletes the fixed dead-factor alias and recreates it before authenticating the new wrap or persisting it. Cancellation/storage failure can leave original envelope bytes pointing at a replaced alias. The surviving factor is retained but the old generation is not fully preserved.

Admission compares generation only after the action returns. Lock can invalidate the operation while auth is suspended; a late success can still delete/create aliases and write the envelope before guarded returns UserCancelled and clears the key. Mutex serialization is per provider instance, not all providers sharing the directory.

Storage mutex is per instance; a second provider can observe the same generation and overwrite shared fixed aliases before stale-version failure. The file write uses legacy best-effort parent-directory sync and no retained generations.

Public contract says the dead alias is deleted only after atomic version bump, but implementation deletes it first. Correct this documentation with the eventual implementation, not by claiming existing safety.
RewrapResult.Success currently requires currentKey nonnull and moves straight to Unlocked. A metadata-only activation result cannot be returned as this success or it would silently grant a session.
Production already narrows prompts per factor and enforces exact CryptoObject Cipher. Keep those rules; this is not permission to broaden authenticators or reduce per-use authentication.

next_slice_29_2_2.deliverable: Internal activation from a selected staged v1-to-v2 transaction, using a freshly supplied candidate, a fresh exclusive closed-vault lease, fresh native proof and fresh authenticated decrypt readbacks of both staged wraps. The outcome never carries key bytes, a token or session authority.

exact_production_files.change: NEW coordinator; consumes/zeros candidate, resolves strict stage paths, proves exact ciphertext snapshot, authenticates both factors and invokes the file primitive only in the same live operation.

Add bounded retained-file/install readback before rename, and explicit observable post-rename/unknown/durability outcomes. Preserve single-use transaction directories and atomic lease check plus active-byte compare/rename.

If required for post-commit checking, add a narrow ciphertext-only assertion; leave assertSourceUnchanged envelope pin intact for every pre-commit authorization check. Do not let the new method substitute for pre-commit validation.

exact_test_files.change: NEW host orchestration, preservation, race and negative-control suite.
Extend readback corruption, failure/lease revocation, post-rename uncertainty and reinspection tests without weakening existing boundary expectations.
Only if the ciphertext-only post-commit check is added; prove old envelope pin still refuses substitution before commit.

excluded_files_and_behavior: No MainActivity, public factory, VaultKeyProvider/UnlockManager or UI changes in this child
No changes to existing preparation or legacy decoder inputs
No DB migration/open/reset; no alias deletion/regeneration during activation
No public activation capability from Prepared, transaction UUID, phase marker or checksum
algorithm: Consume caller candidate immediately into a private copy and zero caller buffer. Acquire production exclusive closed-vault lease; poisoned/uncertain native closure, live key/pool, reset marker, journal or path aliasing refuses before proof or auth.

Strictly read bounded staged old/new bytes through canonical non-symlink paths; directory UUID must equal decoded v2 transaction UUID. Read active exact bytes. First slice accepts only active==staged old and old decodes under the unchanged v1-only decoder. Require generation old+1 without overflow and the same StrongBox policy.

Capture the closed ciphertext DB/WAL/SHM plus active-envelope snapshot and run existing native candidate proof against its private ciphertext copy. A passphrase valid for another export/vault is insufficient.

For each staged v2 factor, obtain its strict UUID alias decrypt Cipher, authenticate exactly that Cipher with factor-specific prompt, then apply that exact record’s AAD and decrypt. Constant-time compare each readback to the freshly proved candidate and zero it. Missing key, invalidation, wrong factor, user cancel, substituted Cipher or wrong readback refuses with all old/new evidence intact.

Immediately before persistence, reassert the original snapshot and lease. Reread stage old/new bytes and compare with frozen validated copies. No async gap may convert Prepared into authority; candidate proof, fresh auth and commit belong to one live invocation.

Durably retain exact old/new copies and install bytes in a new single-use recovery-envelopes UUID directory, with bounded readback of each. Full ciphertext hashes and all fsync calls remain outside the revocation monitor. The final critical section contains only lease validity, bounded active-byte equality and atomic rename.

Treat rename as the activation linearization point, not session unlock. Attempt parent-directory sync and report its durability separately. After any possible rename, never return a result that asserts nothing changed unless exact active bytes prove that under a fresh valid observation. Zero candidate/readbacks on every exit.
Close the lease without populating currentKey or minting AuthorizationToken. A later normal v2 unlock must obtain its own authentication and admission.

crash_state_machine.observation: Prepared files/UUID may exist; no active replacement established
crash_state_machine.allowed: Only new candidate proof plus fresh factor auth can authorize a new commit attempt.

crash_state_machine.observation: Active bytes exactly equal retained old; copies may be partial
crash_state_machine.allowed: Preserve originals. Do not overwrite a used transaction directory; partial attempts remain diagnostic evidence. A separately prepared fresh UUID may be retried with fresh proof/auth.

crash_state_machine.observation: Atomic rename occurred or exact active bytes equal retained new, but directory sync/clean completion is not established
crash_state_machine.allowed: Remain locked, retain all evidence/aliases, report explicit uncertainty. Never automatically roll back or delete either generation.

crash_state_machine.observation: Exact new bytes active and required parent sync completed in the live authorized transaction
crash_state_machine.allowed: Report envelope activation only. Current key/token/session remain absent; normal unlock is separate.

crash_state_machine.observation: Active matches neither retained old/new, evidence missing/corrupt, path mismatch, or cancellation/revocation prevents trusted post-rename inspection
crash_state_machine.allowed: Fail closed; preserve every file/alias, no automatic activation/rollback/reset. Later fresh exclusive observation may classify bytes but cannot confer authentication/session authority.

logical_test_requirements: Prepared-only UUID/phase/checksum cannot call a successful commit; no candidate or wrong candidate produces no auth/rename.
Altered old envelope, DB/WAL/SHM, staged new bytes, generation, UUID/aliases, StrongBox bit, factor AAD and substituted Cipher each fail without active overwrite.
Both-factor fresh auth is required even after earlier preparation authenticated four operations; cancellation/error at either fresh readback never commits.
Source, alias or staged-byte changes between each suspend boundary and final rename invalidate authority; returned readbacks and candidate buffers are zeroed.
Lock/reset/open/other recovery races across separate production instances: late auth cannot publish; no ordinary admission while exclusive work runs; poison refuses before proof/alias activity.
Latch-block full hashing and directory fsync; lock revocation returns without waiting for bulk IO. After revocation the attempt cannot cross the final commit check.
Inject IOException at every durable boundary including install readback, before/after rename and final parent sync. Preserve exact originals and distinguish old/new/unknown; no automatic rollback.
Fresh coordinator instance reinspection of every retained boundary reproduces observation only. Existing tx directory is never reused/erased.
Successful host activation is readable by existing production v2 provider in a separate normally authenticated unlock, while currentKey stays null immediately after activation.
retained_negative_controls: Temporarily substitute a Prepared/UUID-only authorization path: wrong-candidate/no-fresh-auth test must fail; retain exact mutant source and raw failing XML before restoration.
Remove final active-byte/lease check: deterministic changed-active or revoked-lease case must fail without editing assertions.
Remove staged readback/AAD binding: corruption or opposite-factor fixture must fail.
Restore all final source hashes and rerun complete affected dev/foss host suites plus both AndroidTest compilation and lint under root queue. Host failure injection is not power-loss proof.

follow_on_29_2_4.recommended_direction: Replace fixed-alias v1 mutation with the staged v1-to-v2 recovery engine after the activation child is reviewed. A surviving-factor unwrap supplies only a candidate, which still needs closed-vault proof; it never grants mutation permission by itself. Retain both original fixed aliases permanently for this bounded recovery flow.
root_owned_api_integration_files: their focused contract tests; app/feature exhaustive UI handling selected by coordinator
follow_on_29_2_4.dispatch_constraint: Do not hold normal RecoveryKeyAdmission while trying to acquire an exclusive recovery lease, and do not bypass exclusion with an isOpen sample. Build a distinct closed recovery operation. Any shared leased preparation engine must retain stage-only public semantics and never make Prepared a commit capability.
follow_on_29_2_4.contract_decision_before_implementation: Preferred result is ActivatedNeedsNormalUnlock, rather than the old RewrapResult.Success contract that requires an already-live master. Coordinator must choose/update app/session handling explicitly. If preserving automatic unlocked success is required, it needs a separate authenticated admission handoff design and tests; do not infer that permission from activation.
required_tests: Lock during each old/new factor authentication: no fixed-alias deletion, no active-file write after revoked authority
Two provider instances recover concurrently: one exclusive owner, no shared fixed-alias race
Failure/cancel/crash boundaries preserve both old aliases and original envelope/ciphertext
Surviving-factor candidate for wrong ciphertext fails proof
Post-rename interruption reports activation uncertainty without publishing a key/session
Unchanged ordinary v1 unlock/setup and credential fallback regressions remain passed
follow_on_29_2_4.not_a_complete_fix: Adding ensureActive or a late epoch check alone only narrows cancellation races; it cannot make destructive fixed-alias replacement crash-safe and must not close29.2.4.

separate_acceptance.host_implementation: Typed state transitions, ownership, byte preservation, authenticated binding using fakes, native-proof orchestration, negative/race controls and compilation.
separate_acceptance.android_runtime: Actual per-use AndroidKeyStore CryptoObject operations for both factors, StrongBox policy behavior, native encrypted proof, app-process termination/restart and filesystem error behavior with disposable synthetic vaults. No owner reset or owner-vault fixture.
separate_acceptance.app_integration: Explicit locked recovery entry, passphrase/credential candidate routing, cancellation and uncertain-commit wording, activity recreation and normal post-activation unlock. Root owns shared integration.
separate_acceptance.physical: Exactly one appointed Fold runner, current connection and normal owner unlock, separately authorized synthetic fixtures. No implication from host/emulator success.
separate_acceptance.power_loss: Host injected IO exceptions and process restarts are not proof of storage durability under actual power loss; retain this distinction in acceptance.

authorization_boundary: The owner already authorized autonomous development. This proposal does not request renewed owner permission; it awaits coordinator source dispatch/design sequencing and does not itself authorize runtime or owner-vault actions.
